name: ROMANIA
lead: Romania lies in Eastern Europe where Carpathian forests meet a vast river delta on the Black Sea. It holds one of Europe's largest brown bear populations, painted medieval monasteries, and Bran Castle — the fortress behind the Dracula legend. Romanians speak a Latin tongue descended from Roman soldiers who settled here 2,000 years ago.
geo: The Carpathian Mountains curve through Romania like a horseshoe, wrapping the interior in beech and fir forests. Below the peaks, wide plains stretch south and east, watered by the Danube — Europe's second-longest river.

Where the Danube meets the Black Sea it splits into three channels, forming the Danube Delta — a UNESCO wetland the size of a small country. Over 300 bird species nest or stop here, making it one of Europe's greatest wildlife refuges.
animals: Romania is home to over 10,000 brown bears — the largest population in Europe. Wolves, lynx, and chamois share the same Carpathian slopes, rarely seen but always close.
The Danube Delta is a pelican paradise. Great white pelicans and Dalmatian pelicans glide over the reed beds in thousands. Each spring, thousands of white storks nest across Romanian villages.
culture: Romania's craftspeople carve wooden gates so ornate they take months to finish — the ornate gates of Maramureș are celebrated works of folk art. Embroidered blouses called ie inspired Henri Matisse, and every region has its own pattern.

Folk music uses a fiddle, a cobza lute, and a long alphorn called a bucium. Village festivals called hora gather everyone in a circle dance. Romanian food loves polenta (mămăligă), slow stews, and sour soup called ciorbă.
history: Two thousand years ago, Roman legions conquered the Dacian people here, building roads and cities. Latin mixed with the local tongue — and that Roman language is still spoken today as Romanian.

After Ottoman, Habsburg, and Russian rule, Romania united in 1918. Communist dictatorship lasted until 1989, when a dramatic revolution toppled Nicolae Ceaușescu in ten days. Romania joined the EU in 2007.
wows: Roșia Montană's ancient gold landscape became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.
The Parliament Palace in Bucharest is the world's heaviest building at roughly 4 billion kilograms.
Bram Stoker never visited Romania, yet based Dracula's castle on the real Bran Castle in Transylvania.
Nadia Comaneci scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics history at the 1976 Montreal Games.
The Merry Cemetery in Săpânța has colourful wooden crosses with funny poems about each person's death.
Romania has eight UNESCO-listed painted monasteries, with vivid medieval frescoes on every outdoor wall.
Bears regularly wander into mountain towns like Brașov to raid rubbish bins, becoming local celebrities.

myths.fact: Transylvania is a sunny plateau ringed by mountains, famous for medieval walled cities like Sibiu and Sighișoara — far more cheerful than its spooky reputation.
Romanian is a Romance language descended directly from Latin — closer to Italian and Spanish than to Russian or Polish.
